title: Check Current OptiSweep System State in the WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an equivalent approved API client to retrieve and interpret the current system state before assessing lifecycle status.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when live OptiSweep lifecycle status is needed before interpreting system behavior or deciding whether the system is running or shut down. Perform the check on the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or another approved API client.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to start up or shut down the system; those are separate API operations.
Do not use this procedure to infer the meaning of a state that is not explicitly returned by the API.
Do not use this procedure as a training-material orientation or architecture walkthrough.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an approved API client to retrieve and interpret the current system state.
Review or assist when the System State request cannot be executed or does not return a current state.

safety_notes: This procedure uses the GET System State diagnostic request and does not direct the user to execute state-changing API operations.
Do not infer an unlisted state meaning from the returned response.

access_required: Access to the OptiSweep / WCS API.
Access to Apidog or an equivalent approved API client.
system_preconditions: The GET System State request must be available in the System API list.

steps.title: Locate GET System State in the OptiSweep / WCS API
steps.purpose: Identify the diagnostic API operation that returns the current OptiSweep system state.
steps.instruction: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API in Apidog or another approved API client and locate the GET System State request in the System API list.
steps.expected_result: The GET System State request is visible and available to execute in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.healthy_condition: The System API list contains GET System State and the request is available for execution.
steps.failure_condition: GET System State is not present or cannot be selected in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.

actions.label: Open the API client
actions.exact_action: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API in Apidog or an approved API client.

actions.label: Locate the request
actions.exact_action: Locate GET System State in the System API list.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support or the API/system owner if GET System State cannot be located or selected.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Apidog is installed on the primary servers, and the API list includes GET System State.
The System API list includes GET System State.

steps.title: Execute GET System State in the OptiSweep / WCS API
steps.purpose: Retrieve the current live system state from the OptiSweep / WCS API.
steps.instruction: Execute the GET System State request in Apidog or the approved OptiSweep / WCS API client and inspect the returned current system state.
steps.expected_result: The request returns the current live OptiSweep system state.
steps.healthy_condition: A current system state is returned by GET System State and can be read directly from the API response.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be executed or does not return a current system state.

actions.label: Run the state request
actions.exact_action: Execute the GET System State request.

actions.label: Inspect the response
actions.exact_action: Observe the returned current system state.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support or the API/system owner if the GET System State request cannot be executed.
Escalate to L3 support or the API/system owner if the request does not return a current state.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: System State gets the current state of the system.

steps.title: Interpret the returned system state
steps.purpose: Classify the current lifecycle state without assigning unsupported meanings.
steps.instruction: Use the state explicitly returned by GET System State to determine whether the system is in a running state, a shutdown state, or another state explicitly returned by the OptiSweep / WCS API.
steps.expected_result: The returned response is classified as running, shutdown, or another explicitly returned state without inferring an unlisted meaning.
steps.healthy_condition: The API response contains a state that can be identified directly as running, shutdown, or another explicitly returned state.
steps.failure_condition: The response does not identify a current state, or the operator would need to infer the meaning of an unlisted state.

actions.label: Compare the returned state
actions.exact_action: Determine whether the returned system state is running, shutdown, or another state explicitly returned by the API.

actions.label: Avoid unsupported interpretation
actions.exact_action: Do not infer an unlisted state meaning from the API response.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support or the API/system owner if the returned state is unavailable or its meaning is not explicitly defined by the response or supported reference.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: System State gets the current state; System Startup applies when the system is in a shutdown state, and System Shutdown applies when the system is in a running state.

success_criteria: GET System State is available in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
The request returns the current live OptiSweep system state.
The returned state is identified as running, shutdown, or another state explicitly returned by the API without unsupported inference.
healthy_conditions: Apidog or an approved API client displays GET System State in the System API list.
GET System State returns a current state that can be read from the response.
The returned state is explicitly interpretable as running, shutdown, or another returned state.
failure_conditions: GET System State cannot be located or executed.
The API request does not return a current system state.
The returned state is not explicitly interpretable from the available response or source-supported state meanings.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L3 support or the API/system owner if the System State request cannot be executed.
Escalate to L3 support or the API/system owner if no current state is returned.
